message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 150, "amount_cents": 12682}, {"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 150, "amount_cents": 12682}, {"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table contains every requested refund at the requested amount, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds at the requested amounts, so no hold is needed. Next I'll list the orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 9958 cents, which I'll record as its payout. Acme's orders total 18740 + 3900 = 22640, and its refund on order 150 is 12682, so 22640 - 12682 = 9958, which agrees with the figure from net_balance. I'll record the payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get Birch's net balance from the ledger rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance is 42141 cents. Its orders total 25496 + 32515 = 58011, minus the 15870 refund on order 151, which gives 42141, so the ledger figure agrees. I'll record the payout.

Cobalt is the last customer in the batch. Its orders total 36736 + 18321 = 55057, minus the 4209 refund on order 155, which gives 50848. I'll get its net balance from the ledger to confirm before recording.
Cobalt's ledger net is 50848, matching my own check of 55057 - 4209. The refunds were verified, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched my own check against the orders and refunds, and the refunds table covered every requested refund at the requested amount.
